newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH 96 C/A GAP OVER CAP ACC SURPLUS - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH 96 C/A GAP OVER CAP ACC SURPLUS - MINISTER.

text.p: The 1996 Czech current account deficit will probably exceed the capital account surplus by about $1 billion, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Tuesday.

Speaking at a business forum in Prague, Dlouhy said that while there would be a shortfall in 1996, "it is nothing dangerous" for the Czech economy given its current foreign currency reserves of about $16 billion.
"A current account deficit of about one-sixteenth of reserves isn't tragic," he said.
The current account for the first three quarters of 1996 showed a deficit of $3.1 billion while the capital account was in surplus by some $2.0 billion.
Dlouhy said the economy faced two basic problems, neither of which had an easy answer - inflation and the current account deficit which has been spurred by a record trade deficit.

But he said that a devaluation of the crown to help exports, something Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has said he is loathe to do, would not be an easy answer to the problem since it would also have a negative impact on inflation.
He added that wage growth had been a factor in inflation, and has a residual effect on competitiveness, though the trade deficit had micro-economic rathher than macro-economic causes.
This problem required "further developement of the banking sector and the competitiveness of companies", he said.
The trade shortfall stood at 140 billion crowns for the first 11 months of the year, nearly double the 81 billion crown deficit for the same period in 1995.
After making solid progress in previous years, inflation remained stubbornly high for 1996 with the annual average rate easing slightly to 8.8 percent from 9.1 percent in 1995.
A lack of transparency in the capital markets, he added, has hindered investment and must be addressed to keep capital inflows from drying up.
